slides.title: Assistron: Bayesian Shared Autonomy with Off-the-shelf Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.highlight: Assistron reduces human effort by using VLA models for macro-movements and soliciting human intervention at critical failure points, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on human-AI coadaptation and intent alignment.

card.one_liner: Assistron enables shared autonomy by blending frozen VLA models with sparse human interventions during contact-rich tasks.
card.key_idea: A framework using a phase-aware detector to trigger human intervention, which is fused into a frozen VLA's flow-matching process via posterior guidance to avoid fine-tuning.
card.evaluation: Tested on a multi-task scene recovery benchmark with 17 participants; showed 91.3% success and significantly reduced mental/physical workload versus direct teleoperation.
card.limitation: Performance is bounded by the underlying VLA's semantic capabilities and assumes user corrections align with the VLA's action distribution.

slides.title: DexTeleop-0: Force-Aware Bimanual Dexterous Teleoperation with Ego-Centric Perception towards Shared Autonomy
slides.highlight: This work introduces a tactile-driven adaptation strategy that uses real-time optimization to translate human tracking intents into force-compliant robotic commands. The approach improves success rates in contact-rich, high-precision bimanual manipulation tasks by bridging the embodiment gap.

card.one_liner: DexTeleop-0 enables precise bimanual dexterous teleoperation by combining egocentric vision with tactile-driven force optimization.
card.key_idea: A shared autonomy framework that uses a real-time QP optimization loop to translate coarse VR tracking intents into force-compliant robotic commands via operational space Jacobians.
card.evaluation: Evaluated in IsaacSim and on real hardware (UR7e arms, Sharpa Wave hands) across tasks like gear assembly and food sorting; outperformed baselines in success rates.

slides.title: Tactile Genesis: Exploring Tactile Sensors at Scale for Learning Dexterous Tasks
slides.highlight: Tactile Genesis enables large-scale simulation of diverse tactile sensors to determine how sensor type, placement, and resolution affect dexterous manipulation performance.

card.one_liner: Tactile Genesis is a high-throughput GPU simulator for evaluating tactile sensor configurations in dexterous manipulation.
card.key_idea: A parallel simulation platform supporting multiple tactile modalities (force, proximity, temperature, etc.) with configurable resolution, placement, and noise models for large-scale policy training.
card.evaluation: Teacher-student policies on three dexterous tasks, verified via transfer to real XHand1; compared throughput against previous simulators.

slides.title: NoContactNoWorries: Estimating Contact through Vision and Proprioception for In-Hand Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work presents a multimodal framework fusing RGB-D vision and proprioception to infer binary contact states, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception of team states.

card.one_liner: A transformer-based framework that infers binary fingertip contact using RGB-D vision and robot proprioception.
card.key_idea: Fuses RGB-D tokens with current and commanded joint configurations via cross-attention, using a causal transformer to capture temporal dynamics for pseudo-tactile contact estimation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via F1 scores and in-hand reorientation tasks on simulated and real LEAP hands across seen and novel objects; results show robust sim-to-real transfer.
card.limitation: Performance degrades on real hardware for non-convex geometries due to high visual occlusion and sensing noise.

slides.title: Geometric Reconstruction of Extrinsic Contact Trajectories using Tactile Sensing and Proprioception for Tool Manipulation
slides.tldr: RECONSTRUCTING TOOL-TIP CONTACT TRAJECTORIES VIA TACTILE SENSING
slides.highlight: This research proposes a method to reconstruct extrinsic tool-tip contact trajectories by combining tactile sensing and robot proprioception. The approach enables the recovery of contact geometry even when the interaction occurs away from the sensor.

card.one_liner: Reconstructs extrinsic tool-tip contact trajectories using in-hand tactile sensing and robot proprioception.
card.key_idea: A two-stage geometric pipeline: first, anchoring the initial contact point via fixed-point constraints, then propagating it using 6-DoF relative rigid motions estimated via the Kabsch algorithm.
card.evaluation: Evaluated over 51 trials with various tools and trajectories; achieved 8.59mm trajectory RMSE and 5.96mm shape RMSE at 14Hz loop rate.
card.limitation: Assumes a dominant single-point contact and continuous contact, relying on a grooved environment to prevent slip and intermittent contact.

slides.title: BiliVLA: Scene-Aware Vision-Language-Action Model with Reinforcement Learning for Autonomous Biliary Endoscopic Navigation
slides.tldr: AUTONOMOUS BILIARY ENDOSCOPIC NAVIGATION VIA VLA
slides.highlight: BiliVLA utilizes a Vision-Language-Action framework with reinforcement learning to achieve robust autonomous navigation in complex endoscopic environments. This aligns with MIMIC's focus on integrating LLM-based agent models for precise action and perception alignment.

card.one_liner: BiliVLA enables autonomous biliary endoscopic navigation using a scene-aware Vision-Language-Action model and reinforcement learning.
card.key_idea: A two-stage framework combining grounding-enhanced supervised fine-tuning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) to predict target categories, bounding boxes, and discrete 3-DoF motor commands.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on three ERCP subtasks using a real-world phantom; achieved 91.96% action precision and 84.85% success rate, outperforming EndoVLA and Qwen3-VL.
card.limitation: Evaluations were limited to phantom models; further testing on ex vivo tissue and diverse visual degradations is needed.

slides.title: Do Rigid-Body Simulators Dream of Soft Robots? Learning Contact-Rich Manipulation for Tendon-Driven Continuum Robots
slides.tldr: SIM-TO-REAL TRANSFER FOR CONTACT-RICH CONTINUUM ROBOT MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a continuum-mechanics-informed discretization for tendon-driven continuum robots in MuJoCo, enabling sim-to-real transfer for contact-rich tasks. It is relevant to MOSAIC's focus on physics-based skill acquisition and the integration of complex dynamics for human-AI coadaptation.

card.one_liner: Enables sim-to-real transfer for contact-rich manipulation of tendon-driven continuum robots using a physically grounded MuJoCo discretization.
card.key_idea: A continuum-mechanics-informed discretization maps Kirchhoff rod theory to a rigid-body chain in MuJoCo, deriving joint stiffnesses analytically from material properties.
card.evaluation: Validated against Cosserat rod references and real hardware; zero-shot ACT policies achieved ~76-78% success in grasping and switch-flipping tasks.
card.limitation: Validated only on slender, thin-backbone robots; lacks real-time full-shape feedback and comparison with alternative learning architectures.

slides.title: LIBERO-Safety: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Physical and Semantic Safety in Vision-Language-Action Models
slides.highlight: This work introduces a safety benchmark and dataset for Vision-Language-Action models, offering insights into the tension between generalization and safety relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: LIBERO-Safety is a comprehensive benchmark evaluating physical and semantic safety in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models.
card.key_idea: A parametric benchmark using UBDDL for procedural scene generation and a keypose-driven pipeline to synthesize 19,664 collision-free demonstrations via an optimization-based motion planner.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 8 VLA and 2 foundation models across 75 tasks using Success Rate, Collision Rate, and Refusal Rate; results show critical OOD vulnerabilities.
card.limitation: Task success is bottlenecked by sub-optimal trajectory synthesis and semantic misalignment, even when physical safety constraints are maintained.
